items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: You know, I had heard him with Stuff Smith and in '36 I heard

ctx.x: And then I said, you know, I have this sort of system, it was to help a kid that had braces on their teeth, and then I found out it was very good for developing a register and things, basically it's trying to develop a new embouchure because, you know, a person's been playing a certain length of time and they've got a lot of strength, they don't progress, obviously they don't have the right setting on their mouth, then. And I had discovered a way to get around what holds you back from developing. And I said, I…

But I was very enthusiastic about this system, I still am, actually. So we went in, and the big problem. Here's an established musician that I admired, and you know, I had practically made a career out of "Jonah Joins Cab," that record, took a lot of good stuff off that record. You know, I had heard him with Stuff Smith and in '36 I heard

him out at a Famous Door in Hollywood. It was the first time I hever heard a guy play four or five chords in a row, he used to play "Stomping at the Savoy" and end up on a high A-flat. Shake the room, this big, fat sound. He's always been one of my big idols, he's great. And I felt sorry for him.
